proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}shape}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\mbox{-}envelope}\),
\[
 e_P(x)=\frac{r_\kappa(x)g_P(x)}4,
 \qquad 1\le g_P(x)\le2.
\]
If \(\kappa=0\), then \(r_\kappa\equiv1\), and hence \(1/4\le e_P(x)\le1/2\) for every \(x\).  If \(\kappa>0\), then \(r_\kappa(x)>0\) except at the single point \(x=0\), while \(r_\kappa(x)\le1\).  Thus, in either case,
\[
 0<e_P(x)\le\frac12<1
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X\).  The exceptional singleton has probability zero by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\mbox{-}design}\).

Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  On the full-measure set on which \(P(A=a\mid X=x)>0\), consistency gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x,A=a]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x,A=a].
\]
Conditional exchangeability gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x,A=a]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x].
\]
These are equalities of versions of conditional expectations, and hence are asserted only for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).  By the definitions of \(\mu_{a,P}\) and \(\nu_{a,P}\), they imply
\[
 \mu_{a,P}(x)=\nu_{a,P}(x)
 \quad\text{for }P_X\text{-almost every }x.
\]
Both sides are continuous on \(\mathcal X\).  If they differed at some \(x_0\), continuity would give a relatively open neighborhood on which their absolute difference is positive.  Every nonempty relatively open subset of the cube has positive uniform measure, contradicting almost-everywhere equality.  Therefore \(\mu_{a,P}=\nu_{a,P}\) everywhere on \(\mathcal X\).

The observed law determines the almost-everywhere versions of \(\mu_{0,P}\) and \(\mu_{1,P}\).  Two continuous functions on a full-support uniform design that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere by the preceding argument.  Their continuous versions, their difference, and consequently the value at zero of the unique continuous extension \(\tau_P\) are therefore determined by the observed law.  No conditional mean at the null point \(x=0\) was used.

Write \(m_\gamma=\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), let \(v_\gamma(z)\) be the finite vector of all monomials \(z^\nu\) with \(|\nu|\le m_\gamma\), and put \(D=[1/2,1]^d\).  Its Gram matrix
\[
 H_\gamma=\int_Dv_\gamma(z)v_\gamma(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
\]
is positive definite: if \(c^{\mathsf T}H_\gamma c=0\), then the continuous polynomial \(c^{\mathsf T}v_\gamma\) vanishes almost everywhere on \(D\), hence everywhere on the interior of \(D\), and therefore all its coefficients vanish.  Define
\[
 q_\gamma(z)=v_\gamma(0)^{\mathsf T}H_\gamma^{-1}v_\gamma(z).
\]
It follows directly that, for every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(m_\gamma\),
\[
 \int_Dq_\gamma(z)p(z)\,dz=p(0). \tag{1}
\]

The H\"older condition \(\mathrm{ass:contrast\mbox{-}holder}\), applied on each segment from \(0\) to \(x\), gives a polynomial \(p_{P,h}\) of degree at most \(m_\gamma\) such that
\[
 \sup_{z\in D}\left|\tau_P(hz)-p_{P,h}(z)\right|\le C_1h^\gamma,
 \qquad p_{P,h}(0)=\tau_P(0). \tag{2}
\]
For completeness, when \(m_\gamma=0\) this is precisely the defining H\"older inequality.  When \(m_\gamma\ge1\), apply the fundamental theorem of calculus successively to \(t\mapsto\tau_P(thz)\) through order \(m_\gamma\); subtracting the Taylor polynomial leaves an integral of the increment of an order-\(m_\gamma\) derivative.  The defining \((\gamma-m_\gamma)\)-H\"older bound is at most \(L\lVert hz\rVert_\infty^{\gamma-m_\gamma}\), while the remaining \(m_\gamma\) integrations contribute \(\lVert hz\rVert_infty^{m_\gamma}\).  Summing the finitely many multi-indices proves (2), including integer \(\gamma\), for which the order-\((\gamma-1)\) derivatives are Lipschitz.

For \(h\in(0,1]\), let \(D_h=hD\).  The supplied propensity is never inverted outside \(D_h\).  On \(D_h\),
\[
 \frac{h^\kappa}{2^\kappa4}\le e_P(x)\le\frac{h^\kappa}{2},
 \qquad 1-e_P(x)\ge\frac12, \tag{3}
\]
where the first lower bound is also valid at \(\kappa=0\).  Define
\[
 Z_P(O)=\frac{AY}{e_P(X)}-\frac{(1-A)Y}{1-e_P(X)}
\]
on \(\{X\in D_h\}\), and set the summand below to zero off that set.  By \(\mathrm{ass:bernoulli\mbox{-}response}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_P(O)\mid X=x]=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x), \tag{4}
\]
and, using binary \(Y\), (3), and the fact that the two treatment indicators are disjoint,
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_P(O)^2\mid X=x]
 =\frac{\mu_{1,P}(x)}{e_P(x)}+\frac{\mu_{0,P}(x)}{1-e_P(x)}
 \le C_2h^{-\kappa}. \tag{5}
\]
The total oracle estimator is
\[
 \widehat\tau^{e}_{h}
 =\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nh^{-d}q_\gamma(X_i/h)
 \mathbf 1\{X_i\in D_h\}Z_P(O_i)
 \right], \tag{6}
\]
where \(\Pi_I(u)=\min\{\max\{u,\inf I\},\sup I\}\).  Formula (6) is Borel and is defined on every sample; (3) shows that it never divides by zero.  By the known uniform design, (1), (2), and (4), its un-clipped expectation has bias at most
\[
 \left|\int_Dq_\gamma(z)\tau_P(hz)\,dz-\tau_P(0)\right|
 \le \lVert q_\gamma\rVert_{L^1(D)}C_1h^\gamma. \tag{7}
\]
Independence, (5), and the change of variables \(x=hz\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(\widehat\tau^{e}_{h,\mathrm{unclipped}})
 \le\frac1n\int_{D_h}h^{-2d}q_\gamma(x/h)^2C_2h^{-\kappa}\,dx
 \le\frac{C_3}{nh^{d+\kappa}}. \tag{8}
\]
Clipping cannot increase distance to \(\tau_P(0)\in[-3/4,3/4]\).  Therefore (7), (8), and \(\mathbb E|W-\mathbb EW|\le\{\operatorname{Var}(W)\}^{1/2}\) yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_h^e-\tau_P(0)|
 \le C_4\left\{h^\gamma+(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\right\}. \tag{9}
\]
Taking \(h=c_0n^{-1/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\), with a fixed \(c_0\in(0,1]\), proves the asserted oracle upper bound.

For the converse, choose a fixed \(C^\infty\) function \(\psi\) on the cube with \(\psi(0)=1\), \(|\psi|\le1\), and support contained in \([0,1/2]^d\) relative to the cube.  Fix \(g_P\equiv1\), \(e_P=r_\kappa/4\), and \(\mu_{0,P}\equiv1/2\).  For \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), set
\[
 \tau_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon a h^\gamma\psi(x/h),
 \qquad \mu_{1,\varepsilon}(x)=\frac12+\tau_\varepsilon(x), \tag{10}
\]
where \(a>0\) is fixed sufficiently small as a function only of \((d,\gamma,L)\).  Scaling each derivative in the definition of \(\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L)\) shows that the H\"older seminorm of the perturbation in (10) is at most a constant times \(a\); its lower-order derivative suprema are at most the same constant because \(h\le1\).  Thus (10), the constant baseline, and the constant multiplier obey all H\"older restrictions.  Decreasing \(a\) if necessary gives \(1/8\le\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\le7/8\).

These observed laws have genuine causal completions: conditional on \(X=x\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with means \(\mu_{0,P}(x)\) and \(\mu_{1,\varepsilon}(x)\), draw \(A\) independently of them with mean \(e_P(x)\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  Hence both laws, denoted \(P_+\) and \(P_-\), belong to the exact class and give the oracle the same function \(e_P\).

For Bernoulli probabilities \(u,v\in[1/8,7/8]\), direct summation gives
\[
 \chi^2\{\operatorname{Bernoulli}(u),\operatorname{Bernoulli}(v)\}
 =\frac{(u-v)^2}{v(1-v)}\le C_5(u-v)^2. \tag{11}
\]
The treatment and control mechanisms are otherwise identical, so (10), (11), and the uniform design imply
\[
 \chi^2(P_+,P_-)
 \le C_6a^2h^{2\gamma}\int_{[0,h/2]^d}r(x)^\kappa\,dx
 \le C_7a^2h^{2\gamma+d+\kappa}. \tag{12}
\]
Here the last power follows by \(x=hz\); the remaining integral is finite and positive for every \(\kappa\ge0\).  Independence gives the exact identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(P_+^{\otimes n},P_-^{\otimes n})
 =\{1+\chi^2(P_+,P_-)\}^n. \tag{13}
\]
Choose the constant \(c_0\) in \(h=c_0n^{-1/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) small enough that (12)--(13) make the product chi-square divergence at most \(1/4\).  If \(Q\ll R\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(\int|dQ/dR-1|\,dR\) yields
\[
 \lVert Q-R\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,R)};
\]
hence the product total variation is at most \(1/4\).

Finally, put \(\Delta=|\tau_+(0)-\tau_-(0)|=2ah^\gamma\).  For any estimator \(T^e\), the two events \(E_\varepsilon=\{|T^e-\tau_\varepsilon(0)|\ge\Delta/2\}\) cover the sample space pointwise.  Integrating their indicators against the smaller of the two product densities gives
\[
 P_+^{\otimes n}(E_+)+P_-^{\otimes n}(E_-)
 \ge1-\lVert P_+^{\otimes n}-P_-^{\otimes n}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge\frac34.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \max_{\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_\varepsilon}|T^e-\tau_\varepsilon(0)|
 \ge\frac{\Delta}{4}\cdot\frac34\ge c_1h^\gamma.
\]
Taking the infimum over oracle estimators proves the lower bound.  Enlarging constants covers the finitely many choices implicit in the fixed \(c_0\), so both inequalities hold for every \(n\ge2\).  Every constant is independent of \(n\); neither construction uses \(\alpha\), and the constant baseline belongs to every prescribed \(\beta\)-ball.

Let \(D=[1/2,1]^d\), \(D_h=hD\), and, for \(s\in\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}\), let \(v_s\) contain all monomials of total degree at most \(m_s=\lceil s\rceil-1\).  Put
\[
 H_s=\int_Dv_s(z)v_s(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz,
 \qquad \lambda_s=\lambda_{\min}(H_s)>0. \tag{14}
\]
Positive definiteness follows by the polynomial argument in the proof of \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\).  Split the observations deterministically into three blocks \(I_1,I_2,I_3\) whose sizes \(N_j\) differ by at most one.  If \(n<6\), define the estimator to be zero.  The resulting bounded loss is absorbed by increasing the final constant, so below assume \(n\ge6\), in which case \(N_j\ge n/4\).

Define the first-block coefficient and clipped multiplier pilot by
\[
 \widehat c_g
 =H_\alpha^{-1}\frac1{N_1}\sum_{i\in I_1}h^{-d}\mathbf1\{X_i\in D_h\}v_\alpha(X_i/h)
 \frac{4A_i}{r_\kappa(X_i)},
 \qquad
 \widehat g(x)=\Pi_{[1,2]}\{v_\alpha(x/h)^{\mathsf T}\widehat c_g\}, \tag{15}
\]
for \(x\in D_h\).  The ratio in (15) is evaluated only on \(D_h\), where \(r_\kappa>0\).  Since
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\frac{4A}{r_\kappa(X)}\,\middle|\,X=x\right]=g_P(x),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\left[\left.\left(\frac{4A}{r_\kappa(X)}\right)^2\right|X=x\right]
 \le C h^{-\kappa}, \tag{16}
\]
the H\"older Taylor calculation used in (2), the fixed inverse in (14), and independence yield, uniformly on \(D_h\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat g(x)-g_P(x)|^2
 \le C\left\{h^{2\alpha}+(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1}\right\}. \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, the expectation of the empirical vector in (15) is \(\int_Dv_\alpha(z)g_P(hz)\,dz\); its polynomial-approximation bias is \(O(h^\alpha)\), and each entry has variance at most \(C/(N_1h^{d+\kappa})\).  Projection onto \([1,2]\), which contains \(g_P(x)\), cannot increase squared error.

For a symmetric matrix \(M=U\operatorname{diag}(\eta_j)U^{\mathsf T}\), write
\[
 \mathcal F_s(M)=U\operatorname{diag}\{\max(\eta_j,\lambda_s/4)\}U^{\mathsf T}. \tag{18}
\]
This spectral functional is continuous and positive definite even when eigenvalues coincide.  On block \(I_2\), define
\[
 \widehat G_0=\frac1{N_2}\sum_{i\in I_2}h^{-d}\mathbf1\{X_i\in D_h\}(1-A_i)
 v_\beta(X_i/h)v_\beta(X_i/h)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 \widehat s_0=\frac1{N_2}\sum_{i\in I_2}h^{-d}\mathbf1\{X_i\in D_h\}(1-A_i)v_\beta(X_i/h)Y_i,
 \qquad
 \widehat\mu_0(x)=\Pi_{[1/8,7/8]}\{v_\beta(x/h)^{\mathsf T}\mathcal F_\beta(\widehat G_0)^{-1}\widehat s_0\}. \tag{19}
\]
Since \(e_P\le1/2\), the population matrix \(G_0=\int_D(1-e_P(hz))v_\beta v_\beta^{\mathsf T}dz\) satisfies \(G_0\succeq H_\beta/2\).  Every entry of \(\widehat G_0-G_0\) has variance at most \(C/(N_2h^d)\).  Finite dimensionality, Chebyshev's inequality, and the union bound therefore give
\[
 P\{\lVert\widehat G_0-G_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\lambda_\beta/4\}
 \le C(nh^d)^{-1}. \tag{20}
\]
On the complementary event the inverse is uniformly bounded.  Subtracting the scaled Taylor polynomial for \(\mu_{0,P}\) from the normal equation in (19) leaves a deterministic \(O(h^\beta)\) approximation vector and a centered empirical vector with coordinate variance \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\).  On the event in (20), clipping bounds squared error by a constant.  Consequently, uniformly on \(D_h\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\mu_0(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)|^2
 \le C\left\{h^{2\beta}+(nh^d)^{-1}\right\}. \tag{21}
\]

Set \(\widehat e(x)=r_\kappa(x)\widehat g(x)/4\) on \(D_h\).  On the third block, define
\[
 \widehat Q=\frac1{N_3}\sum_{i\in I_3}h^{-d}\mathbf1\{X_i\in D_h\}
 \frac{A_i}{\widehat e(X_i)}v_\gamma(X_i/h)v_\gamma(X_i/h)^{\mathsf T}, \tag{22}
\]
\[
 \widehat b=\frac1{N_3}\sum_{i\in I_3}h^{-d}\mathbf1\{X_i\in D_h\}v_\gamma(X_i/h)
 \left\{\frac{A_i}{\widehat e(X_i)}-\frac{1-A_i}{1-\widehat e(X_i)}\right\}
 \{Y_i-\widehat\mu_0(X_i)\}, \tag{23}
\]
and
\[
 \widehat\tau_h^{(1)}(0)
 =\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left\{v_\gamma(0)^{\mathsf T}
 \mathcal F_\gamma(\widehat Q)^{-1}\widehat b\right\}. \tag{24}
\]
Equations (15), (18)--(19), and (22)--(24) consist of sample moments, fixed finite matrices, continuous spectral flooring, inversion of a matrix whose eigenvalues are bounded below, and clipping.  They thus define a Borel output for every dataset.  Together with the explicit zero fallback for \(n<6\), (24) is total.

It remains to prove its risk.  Conditional on the first two blocks, \(1\le\widehat g\le2\), so on \(D_h\)
\[
 \frac12\le\frac{e_P(x)}{\widehat e(x)}=\frac{g_P(x)}{\widehat g(x)}\le2. \tag{25}
\]
The population counterpart of (22) is therefore at least \(H_\gamma/2\).  Its entries have conditional variance at most \(C/(N_3h^{d+\kappa})\), because \(e_P/\widehat e^{,2}\le Ch^{-\kappa}\) on \(D_h\).  As in (20),
\[
 P\{\lVert\widehat Q-\mathbb E(\widehat Q\mid I_1,I_2)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\lambda_\gamma/4\mid I_1,I_2\}
 \le C(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1}. \tag{26}
\]

For fixed pilots, direct conditioning using \(\mathrm{ass:bernoulli\mbox{-}response}\) gives the exact score identity
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left.
 \left\{\frac A{\widehat e}-\frac{1-A}{1-\widehat e}\right\}(Y-\widehat\mu_0)
 \right|X=x,I_1,I_2\right]
 =\frac{e_P}{\widehat e}\tau_P
 +\frac{e_P-\widehat e}{\widehat e(1-\widehat e)}(\mu_{0,P}-\widehat\mu_0). \tag{27}
\]
Moreover, the multiplier envelope and \(\widehat g\in[1,2]\) imply
\[
 \left|\frac{e_P-\widehat e}{\widehat e(1-\widehat e)}\right|
 \le C|g_P-\widehat g|. \tag{28}
\]
Let \(p_{P,h}\) be the scaled degree-\(m_\gamma\) Taylor polynomial from (2), and let \(c_{P,h}\) be its coefficient vector in the basis \(v_\gamma\).  Subtracting \(\widehat Qc_{P,h}\) from (23), then using (25), (27), (28), and (2), bounds the norm of its conditional mean by
\[
 C h^\gamma+C h^{-d}\int_{D_h}|\widehat g-g_P|\,|\widehat\mu_0-\mu_{0,P}|\,dx. \tag{29}
\]
The two pilot blocks are independent.  Cauchy--Schwarz in probability, followed by (17) and (21), gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[h^{-d}\int_{D_h}|\widehat g-g_P|\,|\widehat\mu_0-\mu_{0,P}|\,dx\right]
 \le C\{h^\alpha+(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\}
       \{h^\beta+(nh^d)^{-1/2}\}. \tag{30}
\]
If \(nh^{d+\kappa}\ge1\), then \(nh^d\ge nh^{d+\kappa}\ge1\), and expansion of (30) yields
\[
 \text{the right side of (30)}
 \le C\left\{h^{\alpha+\beta}+(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\right\}. \tag{31}
\]

Finally, conditional on the pilots, every coordinate of the centered version of \(\widehat b-\widehat Qc_{P,h}\) has variance at most \(C/(nh^{d+\kappa})\): on \(D_h\), all bases, outcomes, pilots, and \(c_{P,h}\) are bounded, and every squared term containing \(A/\widehat e\) has conditional expectation bounded by \(e_P/\widehat e^{,2}\le Ch^{-\kappa}\); the control term is bounded.  Thus its expected Euclidean norm is at most \(C(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\).  On the complement of (26), the inverse in (24) is uniformly bounded.  On the exceptional event, clipping bounds the loss, and (26) contributes at most \(C(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1}\le C(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\).  Combining this fact with (29)--(31), and using that clipping cannot increase distance to \(\tau_P(0)\), proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_h^{(1)}(0)-\tau_P(0)|
 \le C\left\{h^\gamma+h^{\alpha+\beta}+(nh^{d+\kappa})^{-1/2}\right\}. \tag{32}
\]

Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and choose \(h=n^{-1/(2t+d+\kappa)}\).  Then \(nh^{d+\kappa}\ge1\), and every term in (32) is at most \(Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\).  This proves the minimax upper bound because (24) is one admissible data-only estimator.  Conversely, every data-only estimator is an oracle estimator that ignores its supplied propensity, so \(R_n^e\le R_n\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), then \(t=\gamma\), and (32), together with \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\), gives
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}.
\]
This argument uses separate smoothness only for \(g_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), and \(\tau_P\); it never imposes smoothness on \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X]\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: For \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), derive a feasible higher-order data-only risk inequality on the exact class, its matching all-estimator lower bound, the resulting piecewise exponent and every critical logarithmic factor, and the necessary-and-sufficient oracle-penalty partition.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core contains neither a proved higher-order projection inequality nor a fixed-\(n\) full-support mixture comparison. The candidate balance in the frontier handle is editorial evidence rather than a mathematical premise. Estimated-score centering, degenerate projection variance, propensity-dependent Gram stabilization, noninteger corner powers, and max-norm tie surfaces therefore remain uncontrolled on the full class.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the first-order orthogonal score exactly, retained the distinct treated and control effective sample sizes, optimized its bandwidth, and combined it with a genuine same-propensity two-point oracle converse. I also tested the proposed higher-order route against the one-observation mixture algebra; that algebra leaves shared-sign cross-products in the product experiment and therefore cannot certify the conjectured exponent.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  The proved oracle lower bound and the fact that an oracle estimator may ignore \(e_P\), together with the proved data-only first-order estimator, give the uniform all-regime bracket
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}
 \le R_n(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},\qquad n\ge2.
\]
When \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), the two exponents coincide, so \(R_n\asymp R_n^e\) without a logarithmic loss.  For \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), this is an honest, generally nonmatching bracket; neither a rate penalty nor oracle attainment follows from it.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Bound the Hellinger or total-variation distance between the two fixed-\(n\) i.i.d. product mixtures at the nuisance-dominated separation, first for \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), and then in every claimed corner-zero regime, while keeping the covariate distribution exactly uniform and every component law inside the original H\"older class.
open_obligations.obstruction: Averaging the frame signs separately for each observation would prove equality, but that is not the experiment: one latent sign vector indexes the component law and is shared across all \(n\) observations. Consequently the two-observation expansion already contains nonzero overlapping terms involving products of frame signs. No dependency-graph, chi-square, or Hellinger expansion in the frozen core bounds their accumulated fixed-\(n\) contribution at the proposed separation. For \(\kappa>0\), baseline compensation additionally encounters noninteger corner cusps and max-norm tie nonsmoothness.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified the full-support squared-frame construction by expanding the three binary-cell-determining moments. This proves exact one-observation cancellation and legal target separation on the bounded-overlap kill-test slice. Expanding a product likelihood shows why the same calculation cannot be iterated: cross-observation terms retain the common signs. Treating the signs as freshly resampled would change the statistical experiment and is therefore invalid.
open_obligations.partial_result:
On the legal slice \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), choose a smooth bounded-overlap frame \(B_j\) with \(\sum_jB_j(x)^2=V(x)\), independent Rademacher signs \(\lambda_j\), and \(S_\lambda=\sum_j\lambda_jB_j\).  For constants \(p=3/8\), \(m=3/8\), \(t_0=1/8\), amplitudes \(a\asymp\ell^\alpha\), \(b\asymp\ell^\beta\), and \(\delta=2abV\), define
\[
 e_\lambda=p(1+aS_\lambda),\quad
 \mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}=m+\sigma p\delta/2+\sigma(1-p)bS_\lambda,
 \quad \tau_\sigma=t_0-\sigma\delta/2.
\]
Small fixed amplitude constants put every component in the prescribed H\"older balls and interior intervals whenever \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\lesssim h^\gamma\).  Since \(\mathbb E_\lambda S_\lambda=0\) and \(\mathbb E_\lambda S_\lambda^2=V\), direct expansion gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\lambda e_\lambda=p,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_\lambda\{e_\lambda(\mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}+\tau_\sigma)\}=p(m+t_0),
 \quad
 \mathbb E_\lambda\{\mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}+e_\lambda\tau_\sigma\}=m+pt_0.
\]
These three moments determine the four probabilities of the binary pair \((A,Y)\), so the two one-observation mixtures coincide exactly and the contrast separation at zero is \(2ab\) when \(V(0)=1\).  This does not control the fixed-\(n\) product mixtures, because the same \(\lambda\) is shared by all observations and overlapping-frame cross-products survive from the second observation onward.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For \(\kappa=0\) and \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), prove the stated higher-order upper bound and the matching nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform-design class, including the no-log conclusion at \(\alpha+\beta=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The published perforated-support lower construction is not a member of the frozen exact-uniform model, while the supplied full-support construction has only one-observation cancellation and lacks the required product-mixture distance bound. The first-order estimator proved here is slower than the displayed comparator throughout part of the rough-nuisance region and therefore cannot establish the claimed upper inequality there.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the overlap reduction \(e_P\in[1/4,1/2]\), the exact-uniform Bernoulli oracle converse, and the total first-order estimator. These close the displayed comparator theorem when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\). I also checked the squared-frame cancellation route in the rough slice, but its unresolved shared-sign product terms prevent both the exact-class nuisance lower bound and a proof of the theorem as stated.
open_obligations.partial_result:
At \(\kappa=0\), the model assumptions directly give
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
\]
for every \(x\).  Let \(s=\alpha+\beta\).  The established oracle lower bound and first-order estimator imply
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-\min\{\gamma,s\}/(2\min\{\gamma,s\}+d)}.
\]
In particular, if \(s\ge\gamma\), then \(R_n\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\).  In this regime the second term in \(\rho_{n,0}\) is no larger than the first, so the stated bounded-overlap formula is proved, with no logarithmic factor.  The asserted sharper conclusion for every \(s<\gamma\), including its nuisance-dominated lower bound on exactly uniform design, is not supplied by these arguments.
